title: Why you instantly trust people who look like you
hook: Why do we trust some strangers more than others?

narration.text: Your brain tends to favour people who look, think, and act like you.
This is called in-group bias, a natural human tendency.
Our ancestors survived by sticking together in tribes.
Those within our group were seen as safe; outsiders, a potential threat.
This ancient wiring still influences our subconscious decisions today.
It means we often give the benefit of the doubt to people similar to us.
Noticing this bias can help us make fairer judgements.
Have you ever noticed this in yourself or others?

description: Discover the fascinating reason behind why we naturally feel more trusting towards people who resemble us. This psychological phenomenon, known as in-group bias, is deeply rooted in our evolutionary past and continues to shape our social interactions today.
topic: Why you tend to be more trusting of people who look like you, explaining in-group bias.
